memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites: 'Any Israelite or any foreigner residing in Israel who sacrifices any of his children to Molek is to be put to death. The members of the community are to stone him.'" - Lev 20:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter opens with the worst thing a person could do: burn a child alive to buy favour from a god.

Read that again slowly, because our instinct is to hurry past it. Parents placed their own children in the fire. This actually happened, repeatedly, in the culture Israel was entering.

And God responds with absolute severity.

We sometimes wish God were gentler in passages like this. But consider what gentleness would mean here. A God who shrugged at child sacrifice would not be loving. He would be monstrous. The fierceness of His response is the measure of His care for those children.

This is what God's anger actually is. Not a temper. Not cruelty. It is love confronting what destroys the people He made.

Jesus carried the same fire. He welcomed children when His disciples tried to send them away, and He said that anyone who causes one of these little ones to stumble would be better off thrown into the sea with a millstone round their neck (Matt 18:6). That is not gentle language. It comes from the same heart.

If you have ever wondered whether God notices when children are harmed, this chapter is your answer. He notices. He always has.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you thought of God's anger as a flaw rather than an expression of His love?
2. What does His response here tell you about how He values children?
3. Where are children vulnerable today, and what could you do about it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are not indifferent to those who cannot defend themselves. Make me someone who protects the vulnerable as fiercely as You do. Amen.
